concept: Pinned streaming replicated-metadata scan progress and transaction-chain visibility

claims.text: tryFastCommitTxn requires array m when present and uuid/sz/ct fields in every element; unexpected shapes return boost::none. It writes each valid element directly to the output map as it iterates, so its fallback path does not have tryFastApplyOps’s local-map rollback structure. (low confidence)

The introductory comment describes direct CRUD on a fast-count-store namespace as filtered in Layer 1. However, classifyForFastLane routes i/u/d directly to kCrud without a namespace filter, and the fixture named FastLane_DirectCrudOnFastCountStore_NoTimestampAdvance actually constructs a container insert. These source descriptions do not establish general direct-CRUD namespace filtering. (low confidence)

Checkpoint mode emits processed/skipped and processed-size/count metrics. finish erases the oplogUuid delta only when isCheckpoint is true and the scan progress timestamp is absent. A non-checkpoint internal-only scan retains its raw oplog self-delta while leaving the scan progress timestamp absent. (medium confidence)

Fast lanes run only when DeltaAccumulator is not tracking a partial transaction chain. Otherwise records reach typed OplogEntry::parse and DeltaAccumulator, subject to the fallback’s internal-container early return. A missing/non-timestamp ts or non-string op is routed to typed parsing. (low confidence)

The applyOps fast lane inherits outer ui and m when the inner operation lacks them. Nested applyOps, create/drop, truncateRange and other inner shapes outside CRUD/container handling require full dispatch. The typed applyOps function extracts inner OplogEntry objects and recursively calls processOplogEntry. (medium confidence)

When the transaction buffer receives a non-applyOps entry, it clears an active chain and returns no handled count so ordinary typed processing can continue. A prepare applyOps clears any buffered chain and returns zero. Thus those paths do not merge partial contributions into the global result. (low confidence)

The PreparedTxnCommitInvalidatesHash mock-cursor fixture expects the collection hash to be absent after a prepared commit, even when an earlier create and prepared operation supplied hash context. This fixture attributes size/count to the commit without claiming complete transaction hash coverage. (low confidence)

hasPendingWork tests whether lastTimestamp has a value. In checkpoint mode finish erases the oplogUuid delta when that timestamp is absent; the read-mode fixture retains raw self-accounting even for an internal-only stream, while the checkpoint fixture expects an empty result. (high confidence)

When isCheckpoint is true, processed non-internal records emit oplog-processed and size/count-processed metrics, including zero-delta records; skipped internal records emit the skipped metric. These metric calls are conditional in consumeRecord. (high confidence)

When a linked non-partial, non-prepared terminal applyOps reaches an active TxnDeltaBuffer, the buffer processes it into the private deltas, merges those deltas into the global result, and clears the chain. The terminal-entry mock fixture expects the sum of both partial records and the terminal record. (high confidence)

The streaming accumulator requires records in strictly increasing oplog RecordId/timestamp order, with partial applyOps before the terminal entry. It represents one forward scan; consumeRecord or finish after finish is a programming error. The typed path contains a timestamp-order dassert; this is a caller ordering contract, not a sorting operation. (high confidence)

The fast-CRUD hash-only comment describes typed reporting and skipping, whereas the typed implementation and raw fixture describe warning and folding h with zero size/count when ui exists. Without a UUID typed hash-only extraction returns no contribution. These are explicitly different source descriptions; the skip comment must not replace the executable behavior. (high confidence)

With no active partial chain, tryFastApplyOps handles simple inner CRUD and container operations. Missing inner ui and m inherit the outer fields. Nested applyOps, inner DDL, unsupported inner op shapes, and CRUD shapes the helper cannot handle request typed fallback. (low confidence)

TxnDeltaBuffer stores partial applyOps deltas privately and remembers the last OpTime. Continuity of an active chain requires the next applyOps entry.getPrevWriteOpTimeInTransaction() value to exist and equal that stored OpTime; the conflict predicate compares this link rather than session or transaction-number fields. (low confidence)

CRUD with no m is handled as processed with no delta. Object m with neither sz nor h also returns zero. Non-object m, non-numeric sz or h, a non-string namespace, or missing ui for an otherwise eligible sized operation requests typed fallback; UUID parsing can raise rather than return fallback. (high confidence)

A prepared applyOps clears any active private chain and contributes zero. Prepared commit visibility uses commitTransaction metadata instead of the discarded partial or prepare-entry contributions; the MultiEntryPreparedTxnUsesCommitSizeMetadataNotPartialAccumulation fixture explicitly attributes authority to commit metadata. (high confidence)

Unlike the local-map applyOps fast pass, tryFastCommitTxn writes each accepted member directly into the destination map before checking later members. A later malformed member can therefore request fallback after earlier mutations; the source does not implement an all-or-nothing staging map for that helper. (low confidence)

mergeDeltas preserves a created collection state and records its buffered metadata when size, count, or hash differs from the empty-collection identity; it rejects a buffered dropped state with tassert 12406403. The chained create/same-size-update fixture specifically expects the hash-only update contribution to survive the merge. (high confidence)

extractScanFields fatally rejects a tid field with fassertFailed(12565801), because its fast-scan namespace logic does not handle tenant prefixing or tid inheritance. The same extractor is called for inner fast applyOps operations. The death fixture names this unsupported raw shape; this is a fast-extractor boundary rather than a universal tenant-shape validation claim for every typed path. (high confidence)

Before parsing or filtering a record, consumeRecord attributes rec.data.size() bytes and one record to the supplied oplogUuid. Internal fast-count container records therefore still contribute to physical oplog self-accounting, as the OplogUuid_TrackedEvenForInternalEntries fixture asserts. (high confidence)

Container operations on a replicated-fast-count ident take kFastCountStoreSkip without advancing lastTimestamp. In checkpoint mode that branch records a skipped-entry metric. The typed fallback also returns early for isContainerOpOnFastCountIdent before transaction-buffer consumption. (high confidence)

A scanned entry can advance lastTimestamp without producing a user-collection delta: kCountedNoDelta handles ordinary no-ops, unrelated commands, key material, and non-internal container operations. hasPendingWork tests only whether lastTimestamp has a value. (medium confidence)

aggregateReplicatedMetadataDeltasInOplog converts seekAfterTS to a long-format RecordId, seeks with BoundInclusion::kExclude, consumes that record and successive oplogCursor.next records, then returns finish. The mock-cursor AggregateMixedCrudAndApplyOps fixture asserts that seeking after its first insert excludes that insert. (medium confidence)

extractScanFields makes one forward pass over raw BSON and captures op, ns, ui, m, o, o2, ts and container. A tid field encountered by this extractor invokes fassertFailed(12565801); its comment says tenant prefixing and tid inheritance are unsupported on the fast path. (medium confidence)

For command entries the fast classifier examines the first field of o. applyOps and commitTransaction select dedicated lanes; create, drop, truncateRange, and importCollection select typed parsing. Other command names, including unknown ones, are deliberately classified as unrelated no-delta commands. (low confidence)

tryRecordFastCrud returns zero for absent m, or for object m with neither sz nor h. Non-object m, nonnumeric sz or h, missing string namespace, and missing ui on an otherwise eligible size-bearing operation fall through. For a handled i/u/d operation it records sz plus count +1/0/-1 and an optional h. (low confidence)

Typed single-operation extraction returns no contribution for absent metadata, the multi-operation metadata variant, ineligible namespaces, or unsupported operation types. Sized eligible CRUD requires ui through massert 12116001. The utility fixtures separately assert opt-out, wrong metadata variant, and ineligible hash-only behavior. (high confidence)

tryFastApplyOps returns processed zero for prepare before checking partialTxn. A partialTxn entry falls through to seed typed transaction buffering. Simple non-partial inner CRUD and container operations can use this specialized lane. (low confidence)

tryFastApplyOps accumulates inner CRUD in localDeltas and copies it to the global result only after the whole fast pass succeeds. A later unsupported inner operation discards that local map before typed processing reprocesses the outer entry, avoiding double counting of the earlier fast CRUD contributions. (low confidence)

In the non-partial applyOps fast lane, internal fast-count-ident container operations are skipped. If no non-internal inner operation is seen, kAllInternal suppresses timestamp progress; a mixed internal-container/user-CRUD entry records the user contribution and advances the outer timestamp. Non-internal container operations produce no delta but establish progress. (high confidence)

A non-partial, non-preparing applyOps that continues an active chain is processed into the private map, then mergeDeltas transfers the map into globalResult and the chain is cleared. Without an active chain, the buffer returns boost::none for ordinary typed processing. (medium confidence)

An unfinished partial chain contributes no collection deltas to the returned scan result, including its buffered hashes, but lastTimestamp still advances to the last scanned non-internal partial entry. finish returns only the global result; it does not flush the private transaction buffer. (high confidence)

The mock-cursor NotPreparedChainAccountedForAtTerminalEntry fixture combines two partial entries and a terminal entry, expecting the combined size/count at the terminal timestamp. Separate mock-cursor fixtures expect no collection deltas after prepare without commit, prepare followed by abort, and partial-chain abort without prepare. (low confidence)

For a prepared transaction, the mock-cursor MultiEntryPreparedTxnUsesCommitSizeMetadataNotPartialAccumulation fixture deliberately gives commit metadata a value different from the partial sum and expects the commit’s metadata. Both fast and typed commit extraction record size/count with hash absent, and absent commit metadata contributes zero. (medium confidence)

The streaming fixture has two distinct input helpers: runAccumulator drains OplogCursorMock into consumeRecord, whereas runAccumulatorRaw constructs Record values directly from hand-shaped BSON and bypasses the typed-entry round trip. Its convenience helpers erase oplog self-deltas for per-collection assertions. The utility aggregation fixture likewise erases the supplied oplog UUID after calling the cursor aggregation helper. (high confidence)

aggregateReplicatedMetadataDeltasInOplog converts seekAfterTS to a long-format RecordId, seeks with BoundInclusion::kExclude, consumes the returned record and successive next records, and finishes at cursor exhaustion. The AggregateSingleColl mock-cursor fixture expects seeking after an entry to exclude it and seeking at the last entry to yield no deltas. (high confidence)

Ordinary noops, unrelated commands, key-material operations, and container operations on other idents can advance lastTimestamp while producing no per-collection metadata delta. The noop, unrelated-command, and user-ident container fixtures explicitly expect timestamp progress with empty per-collection results. (high confidence)

extractScanFields walks raw BSON once and captures op, ns, ui, m, o, o2, ts, and container. classifyForFastLane requires a real BSON timestamp and string op before dispatch; malformed or missing timestamps fall back to OplogEntry::parse, with rejection expectations in the malformed-CRUD and missing-noop-timestamp fixtures. (high confidence)

For eligible CRUD with object metadata m and numeric sz, tryRecordFastCrud requires a namespace string and UUID, uses the size delta, and derives count as 1 for insert, 0 for update, and -1 for delete. A present numeric h is included; repeated collection contributions accumulate by UUID. The raw two-CRUD fixture expects additive size/count and XOR-folded hashes. (high confidence)

An absent h on a sized operation is represented as an absent hash contribution. The utility fixtures assert that this makes an accumulated collection hash absent while size/count continue accumulating, and later ordinary hash-bearing operations do not restore it. (high confidence)

The fast applyOps path treats prepare as processed with zero contribution, so its timestamp advances. partialTxn requests typed parsing to begin buffering. While a chain is active, consumeRecord bypasses fast lanes so typed accumulation can resolve transaction-chain visibility. (high confidence)

Typed processOplogEntry dispatches commitTransaction and applyOps before the other operation cases. Typed applyOps extraction uses ApplyOps::extractOperationsTo and recursively calls processOplogEntry for the extracted operations, providing the fallback dispatch for nested applyOps and inner operations outside the fast subset. (high confidence)

A non-applyOps record that reaches TxnDeltaBuffer clears an active chain and returns control to ordinary processing. An applyOps with a conflicting or missing previous OpTime clears the old chain before handling the new entry. The interruption fixtures expect the partial contribution to disappear while the later ordinary insert remains visible. (high confidence)

consumeRecord performs typed internal-container filtering before invoking DeltaAccumulator. Consequently an internal fast-count container record returning at that filter does not reach the chain-discard logic, even though active-chain records bypass the raw fast lanes. (low confidence)

The commit fast lane handles absent m as zero contribution, otherwise expects an array whose members provide uuid, sz, and ct, and records per-UUID size/count with hash absent. Unexpected array/member shapes request typed fallback. Typed commit extraction requires the multi-operation metadata variant and also records an absent hash; the prepared-commit hash fixture expects absence. (high confidence)

The no-session mock-cursor fixtures describe large batched partialTxn chains tracked through prevOpTime linkage: the terminal-entry case expects accumulated deletes, and the end-of-log case expects no collection contribution with progress at the final partial timestamp. (high confidence)

The fixture named FastLane_DirectCrudOnFastCountStore_NoTimestampAdvance actually constructs makeContainerOplogEntry with kContainerInsert and the fast-count ident. Its expectation therefore documents a container record, and should not be generalized into evidence that the fixture exercises a raw i/u/d namespace-filter path. (low confidence)
